title: TexasState vs UNT: tuition, size, accreditation
summary: Texas State University (TexasState) versus University of North Texas Health Science Center (UNT). Also searched as UNT vs TexasState. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Texas State University and the University of North Texas Health Science Center (TexasState vs UNT) are both public institutions but differ significantly in size and location. Texas State University, located in San Marcos, has an undergraduate enrollment of 36,177 students, whereas the University of North Texas Health Science Center in Fort Worth enrolls only 41 undergraduates. Additionally, Texas State University charges an in-state tuition of $11,450, while tuition information for in-state students at the University of North Texas Health Science Center is not specified. These differences highlight the distinct scale and focus of each institution.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance, Texas State University and the University of North Texas Health Science Center (TexasState vs UNT) show notable differences. In contrast, tuition data for the University of North Texas Health Science Center is not provided. Additionally, the median debt for students completing their programs at Texas State University is $21,000, while no comparable data is available for the University of North Texas Health Science Center. These figures reflect the financial commitments associated with attending each institution.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus

These differences in campus size and location contribute to varied educational models and student engagement opportunities at each institution.

sections.heading: Pick TexasState if
paragraphs: Pick Texas State University if you prefer a public institution with a high admission rate, as it admits approximately 89.32% of applicants. These factors make Texas State University a suitable choice for students seeking accessible admission and affordable tuition in a large public university setting.
